risks.text: Membership changes must go through /v1/people/:id; better-auth's update-member-role, leave and remove-member are refused in the before-hook, and invite roles must match role names exactly, so calling them from a new client returns 403.

Callers without full member CRUD cannot assign privileged built-in roles or custom roles that hold permissions they lack; new role-editing paths must call validateAssignableRoles or they reopen privilege escalation.

A webhook that verifies a signature only gets req.rawBody if its path is in RAW_BODY_PATHS in main.ts (stripe billing, background checks, pentest); a new signed webhook not listed there fails verification because the body was already parsed.
load-env.ts loads .env with dotenv override:true, so a local .env beats shell or host variables; a stale .env silently wins over what you export.

The 2FA take-over classifier (login outcome and two-factor method) is an LLM call whose values (code, passkey, passkey_only, other) drive the app's take-over wording; 'passkey' must only be returned when a code method exists, and it runs on needs_2fa, challenge and unknown outcomes; changing a value means changing ConnectVendorLoginFlow too.

risks.text: The revalidate route compares the posted secret with !== against REVALIDATION_SECRET, which env.mjs only requires to be a string and .env.example ships as empty, so an empty secret revalidates any path for anyone; use a non-empty minimum and a constant-time compare.

Design-system Select inside a Radix modal Dialog is unclickable unless portal={false} is passed (ConnectionVariablesForm), but the same change on the in-popover people selects broke positioning and was reverted; do not copy portal={false} between the two cases.
The owner-role removal check in the people table is UX only; role authority is enforced by the API, so do not add role rules here without the matching API check.

Connect-vendor-login flow resumes from saved client state (clearConnectState) and shows a resume strip rather than reopening full screen; starting a new connect must clear the old state or it resumes a stale draft, and the take-over copy depends on the API's twoFactorMethod values.
Tailwind class names built from pieces (bg-${accent}-50) are not generated, so the colors vanish in the build; use full class names or a lookup map.

risks.text: The root Dockerfile migrator stage installs prisma ^6.14.0 and the published @trycompai/db ^1.3.4, then copies local migrations into its dist and runs `prisma migrate deploy` against that published schema, while packages/db uses prisma 7.6.0; a migration needing newer Prisma or an unpublished schema change fails at deploy.

Bun 1.4.4 is pinned in packageManager and every Dockerfile stage, and bunfig.toml (hoisted linker) must be copied before bun install; without it Bun 1.3+ makes isolated installs and the later image stages cannot find node_modules.
NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are baked into the app and portal at image build time via Dockerfile ARG; a new browser-visible variable needs an ARG/ENV here and a rebuild, not just a runtime env.
turbo globalEnv lists the env vars that invalidate cached builds; a new env var missing there is ignored by turbo cache and can ship stale builds.

groups.title: Shared VS Code editor settings

rules.rule: Every customer-facing API endpoint has @UseGuards(HybridAuthGuard, PermissionGuard) and @RequirePermission, and controllers use @Controller({path,version:'1'}) not 'v1/x'.
rules.why: Without them the endpoint is unprotected or unlogged for customers and MCP clients; AuditLogInterceptor only records mutations that carry permission metadata; 'v1/x' double-prefixes the route.

rules.rule: Every Prisma query, including raw SQL, filters by the organizationId from the auth context, never from client input.
rules.why: A missing filter lets one customer read or change another customer's data.

rules.rule: Frontends never run their own better-auth instance; sessions come from the API and raw fetches to it send credentials:'include'.
rules.why: A local instance forks sessions and cookies, and a fetch without credentials gets 401.

rules.rule: Role and membership changes go through /v1/people/:id, not better-auth's membership routes.
rules.why: The API refuses those routes and the people endpoints apply the role-escalation checks, so bypassing them either fails or would allow privilege escalation.

checks.why: membership policy and role assignment specs

rules.rule: Signed webhook paths are listed in RAW_BODY_PATHS and handlers claim each event id before processing.
rules.why: Signature checks need the exact bytes, and providers resend events; without the claim a replay double-applies billing.

rules.rule: Role and permission definitions live only in packages/auth/src/permissions.ts; API guards and app route gating read from it.
rules.why: Hardcoded copies drift and users get access in one app that the other denies.

rules.rule: The Prisma schema is edited only in packages/db/prisma/schema and the app copies are regenerated.
rules.why: Apps compile against a stale client or fail the schema check, and migrations then disagree with the schema.

rules.rule: After adding or changing an endpoint, boot the API in dev, commit the regenerated packages/docs/openapi.json, and give each public operation a summary and description.
rules.why: The Speakeasy job builds @trycompai/mcp-server from that file; a stale file means customers never get the tool, and openapi-docs.spec.ts fails the build on a missing description.

rules.rule: Bun 1.4.4, Node 22.23.4 images and Trigger.dev 4.7.7 are bumped together across package.json, Dockerfiles and workflows.
rules.why: Deployed tasks and images that fall back to an older runtime ship the Brotli decoder bug (CVE-2026-111497).

rules.rule: The MCP serve command refuses unsupported request encodings before express.json and requires an API key off loopback.
rules.why: A crafted Brotli body would reach the vulnerable decoder, and an unauthenticated non-loopback server would expose customer tools.
